"""Inline text parsing for code spans, escapes, references, and soft breaks."""

from dataclasses import dataclass
import html.entities
import re


@dataclass
class Inline:
    """An inline text node or a soft line break."""

    type: str
    literal: str = ""
    destination: str = ""
    label: str = ""
    children: list["Inline"] | None = None


_ENTITY = re.compile(r"&(?:#[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6}|#[0-9]{1,7}|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+);")
_ASCII_PUNCTUATION = frozenset("!\"#$%&'()*+,-./:;<=>?@[\\]^_`{|}~")
_C1 = {
    0x80: 0x20AC, 0x82: 0x201A, 0x83: 0x0192, 0x84: 0x201E,
    0x85: 0x2026, 0x86: 0x2020, 0x87: 0x2021, 0x88: 0x02C6,
    0x89: 0x2030, 0x8A: 0x0160, 0x8B: 0x2039, 0x8C: 0x0152,
    0x8E: 0x017D, 0x91: 0x2018, 0x92: 0x2019, 0x93: 0x201C,
    0x94: 0x201D, 0x95: 0x2022, 0x96: 0x2013, 0x97: 0x2014,
    0x98: 0x02DC, 0x99: 0x2122, 0x9A: 0x0161, 0x9B: 0x203A,
    0x9C: 0x0153, 0x9E: 0x017E, 0x9F: 0x0178,
}


def _reference(match: re.Match[str]) -> str:
    token = match.group()
    if token.startswith("&#"):
        body = token[2:-1]
        try:
            value = int(body[1:], 16) if body[:1] in "xX" else int(body, 10)
        except ValueError:
            return token
        if value == 0 or value > 0x10FFFF or 0xD800 <= value <= 0xDFFF:
            value = 0xFFFD
        else:
            value = _C1.get(value, value)
        return chr(value)
    return html.entities.html5.get(token[1:], token)


def parse_inlines(source: str, references: dict) -> list[Inline]:
    """Parse code spans, ordinary text, punctuation escapes, references, and breaks."""
    del references  # Reserved for reference-link parsing in the inline pipeline.
    nodes: list[Inline] = []
    text: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if text:
            value = "".join(text)
            if value:
                nodes.append(Inline("text", value))
            text.clear()

    i = 0
    while i < len(source):
        char = source[i]
        if char == "`":
            run_end = i + 1
            while run_end < len(source) and source[run_end] == "`":
                run_end += 1
            run_length = run_end - i
            search = run_end
            close_start = close_end = -1
            while search < len(source):
                candidate = source.find("`", search)
                if candidate < 0:
                    break
                candidate_end = candidate + 1
                while candidate_end < len(source) and source[candidate_end] == "`":
                    candidate_end += 1
                if candidate_end - candidate == run_length:
                    close_start, close_end = candidate, candidate_end
                    break
                search = candidate_end
            if close_start >= 0:
                flush()
                literal = source[run_end:close_start].replace("\r\n", "\n").replace("\r", "\n").replace("\n", " ")
                # CommonMark normalizes every whitespace run in code spans to
                # one space before applying the surrounding-space rule.
                literal = re.sub(r"(?<=\S)[ \t\n\r]+(?=\S)", " ", literal)
                if len(literal) >= 2 and literal.startswith(" ") and literal.endswith(" ") and literal.strip(" "):
                    literal = literal[1:-1]
                nodes.append(Inline("code", literal))
                i = close_end
            else:
                text.append(source[i:run_end])
                i = run_end
        elif char == "\\" and i + 1 < len(source) and source[i + 1] in _ASCII_PUNCTUATION:
            flush()
            # Keep escaped punctuation opaque to later delimiter processing.
            nodes.append(Inline("escaped", source[i + 1]))
            i += 2
        elif char == "&":
            match = _ENTITY.match(source, i)
            if match:
                decoded = _reference(match)
                if any(delimiter in decoded for delimiter in "*_"):
                    flush()
                    nodes.append(Inline("entity", decoded))
                else:
                    text.append(decoded)
                i = match.end()
            else:
                text.append(char)
                i += 1
        elif char == "\n":
            while text and text[-1] == " ":
                text.pop()
            while i + 1 < len(source) and source[i + 1] == " ":
                i += 1
            flush()
            nodes.append(Inline("softbreak"))
            i += 1
        else:
            text.append(char)
            i += 1
    flush()
    # Delimiter runs may pair across a soft line break. Preserve the public
    # softbreak nodes unless resolving the joined source proves the break is
    # inside emphasis, in which case the newline belongs to that inline node.
    joined: list[Inline] = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node.type == "softbreak":
            if joined and joined[-1].type == "text":
                joined[-1].literal += "\n"
            else:
                joined.append(Inline("text", "\n"))
        elif node.type == "text" and joined and joined[-1].type == "text":
            joined[-1].literal += node.literal
        else:
            joined.append(Inline(node.type, node.literal, children=node.children))
    resolved = _parse_emphasis(joined)
    if any(_contains_emphasis_newline(node) for node in resolved):
        return resolved
    return _parse_emphasis(nodes)


def _contains_emphasis_newline(node: Inline) -> bool:
    return node.type in {"em", "strong"} and (
        "\n" in node.literal or any(_contains_emphasis_newline(child) for child in node.children or [])
        or any(child.type == "text" and "\n" in child.literal for child in node.children or [])
    )


def _parse_emphasis(nodes: list[Inline]) -> list[Inline]:
    """Resolve delimiter runs in text nodes, leaving code spans opaque."""
    result: list[Inline] = []
    for node in nodes:
        if node.type != "text":
            result.append(node)
            continue
        source = node.literal
        # Match valid flanking pairs from the inside out. The pass only handles
        # delimiter characters; punctuation and Unicode whitespace use the
        # same flanking predicates as the CommonMark delimiter rules.
        chunks: list[Inline] = []
        i = 0
        plain = 0
        while i < len(source):
            if source[i] not in "*_":
                i += 1
                continue
            end = i + 1
            while end < len(source) and source[end] == source[i]:
                end += 1
            marker, length = source[i], end - i
            before = source[i - 1] if i else "\n"
            after = source[end] if end < len(source) else "\n"
            opener = not after.isspace() and (not _punct(after) or before.isspace() or _punct(before))
            closer = not before.isspace() and (not _punct(before) or after.isspace() or _punct(after))
            if marker == "_":
                opener = opener and (not closer or _punct(before))
                closer = closer and (not opener or _punct(after))
            if not opener:
                i = end
                continue
            close = end
            found = None
            while close < len(source):
                candidate = source.find(marker, close)
                if candidate < 0:
                    break
                ce = candidate + 1
                while ce < len(source) and source[ce] == marker:
                    ce += 1
                cb = source[candidate - 1] if candidate else "\n"
                ca = source[ce] if ce < len(source) else "\n"
                can_close = not cb.isspace() and (not _punct(cb) or ca.isspace() or _punct(ca))
                if marker == "_":
                    # Intraword underscores cannot close emphasis (the opener
                    # check already applies the corresponding left-flanking rule).
                    can_close = can_close and not (cb.isalnum() and ca.isalnum())
                use = 2 if length >= 2 and ce - candidate >= 2 else 1
                if can_close and candidate > end and not (marker == "_" and before.isalnum() and ca.isalnum()):
                    found = (candidate, ce, use)
                    break
                close = ce
            if found is None:
                i = end
                continue
            a, b, use = found
            prefix = source[plain:i] + marker * (length - use)
            if prefix:
                chunks.append(Inline("text", prefix))
            inner = _parse_emphasis([Inline("text", source[end:a])])
            chunks.append(Inline("strong" if use == 2 else "em", children=inner))
            source = source[:i] + source[end:a] + source[b:]
            i = i + (a - end)
            plain = i
        tail = source[plain:]
        if tail:
            chunks.append(Inline("text", tail))
        result.extend(chunks or [node])
    return result


def _punct(char: str) -> bool:
    return bool(char) and (char in _ASCII_PUNCTUATION or __import__("unicodedata").category(char).startswith("P"))

@dataclass
class Block:
    """A minimal block node retaining source for later inline parsing."""

    kind: str
    children: list["Block"] = field(default_factory=list)
    literal: str = ""
    level: int | None = None
    info: str = ""
    ordered: bool = False
    start: int = 1
    tight: bool = True

    @property

        """Compatibility name for the block node's kind."""

@dataclass
class Document:
    """Ordered block tree and document-wide reference definitions."""

    children: list[Block] = field(default_factory=list)
    references: dict[str, object] = field(default_factory=dict)


def _thematic(line: str) -> bool:
    match = re.fullmatch(r" {0,3}([*_\-])(?:[ \t]*\1){2,}[ \t]*", line)
    return bool(match)


def _atx(line: str):
    match = re.match(r"^ {0,3}(#{1,6})(?:[ \t]+(.*)|[ \t]*$)", line)
    if not match:
        return None
    content = match.group(2) or ""
    if re.fullmatch(r"#+[ \t]*", content):
        content = ""
    content = re.sub(r"[ \t]+#+[ \t]*$", "", content).strip(" \t")
    return len(match.group(1)), content


def _quote_content(line: str) -> tuple[str, bool] | None:
    """Return quote content and whether the marked line is blank."""
    indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" "))
    if indent > 3 or indent >= len(line) or line[indent] != ">":
        return None
    content = line[indent + 1:]
    # A single following space is part of the marker. A tab advances to the
    # next four-column stop; consume one column for the marker and retain the
    # remaining columns so indented code sees the original indentation.
    if content.startswith(" "):
        content = content[1:]
    elif content.startswith("\t"):
        # The tab begins one column after the marker, so it occupies three
        # columns in the source. The marker consumes one; remaining tabs keep
        # their original four-column stops, represented as spaces here.
        rest = content[1:]
        if rest.startswith("\t"):
            rest = "    " + rest[1:]
        content = "  " + rest.expandtabs(4)
    return content, not content.strip(" \t")


_LIST_MARKER = re.compile(r"^( {0,3})([-+*]|([0-9]{1,9})([.)]))([ \t]+|$)(.*)$")


def _list_marker(line: str):
    match = _LIST_MARKER.match(line)
    if not match:
        return None
    indent, marker, digits, delimiter, whitespace, rest = match.groups()
    if marker in "-*+" and _thematic(line):
        return None
    if marker in "*+" and re.fullmatch(r" {0,3}[ *_-](?:[ \t]*[ *_-]){2,}[ \t]*", line):
        return None
    ordered = digits is not None
    start = int(digits) if ordered else 1
    if ordered and start > 999999999:
        return None
    width = len(indent) + len(marker)
    # The marker starts after ``indent`` columns. Tab stops are measured from
    # the beginning of the original line, so expanding the whitespace alone
    # from column zero overcounts tabs after a list marker.
    marker_column = len(indent) + len(marker)
    pad = 0
    for char in whitespace:
        pad += 4 - (marker_column + pad) % 4 if char == "\t" else 1
    if rest and pad > 4:
        rest = " " * (pad - 1) + rest
        pad = 1
    else:
        pad = max(1, pad)
    if not rest.strip(" \t"):
        pad = 1
    return (len(indent), marker if not ordered else delimiter, ordered, start, width + pad, rest, bool(rest.strip(" \t")))


def parse_blocks(markdown: str) -> Document:
    """Parse supported block structures, retaining inline source where needed."""
    document = Document()
    paragraph: list[str] = []

    def finish_paragraph() -> None:
        if not paragraph:
            return
        # Continuation indentation is structural, while trailing whitespace on
        # those lines remains available to the inline parser (for hard breaks).
        lines = [paragraph[0].lstrip(" \t")]
        lines.extend(line.lstrip(" \t") for line in paragraph[1:])
        literal = "\n".join(lines).rstrip(" \t")
        literal = extract_definitions(literal + "\n", document.references).rstrip("\n")
        if literal:
            document.children.append(Block(kind="paragraph", literal=literal))
        paragraph.clear()

    lines = markdown.splitlines()
    i = 0
    while i < len(lines):
        line = lines[i]
        quote_line = _quote_content(line)
        if quote_line:
            finish_paragraph()
            quote_lines: list[str] = []
            has_paragraph = False
            lazy_setext_line: str | None = None
            while i < len(lines):
                marked = _quote_content(lines[i])
                if marked:
                    content, blank = marked
                    quote_lines.append(content)
                    # Lazy continuation is only valid after an open paragraph.
                    # A code block opener or an indented code line closes that
                    # paragraph even though the marked line itself is nonblank.
                    has_paragraph = bool(content.strip(" \t")) and not (
                        parse_fenced_code([content]) is not None
                        or (len(content) - len(content.lstrip(" ")) >= 4)
                    )
                    i += 1
                    continue
                # Blank lines without a marker close the quote. Missing quote
                # markers are lazy only while a paragraph is open.
                if not lines[i].strip(" \t"):
                    break
                if not has_paragraph:
                    break
                if _thematic(lines[i]) or _atx(lines[i]) or _list_marker(lines[i]) or parse_fenced_code(lines[i:]) or parse_html_block(lines[i:]):
                    break
                if quote_lines and parse_setext([quote_lines[-1], lines[i]]):
                    lazy_setext_line = lines[i]
                quote_lines.append(lines[i])
                i += 1
            child_doc = parse_blocks("\n".join(quote_lines))
            if lazy_setext_line is not None and child_doc.children and child_doc.children[-1].kind == "heading":
                heading = child_doc.children[-1]
                child_doc.children[-1] = Block(kind="paragraph", literal=heading.literal + "\n" + lazy_setext_line)
            document.references.update(child_doc.references)
            document.children.append(Block(kind="block_quote", children=child_doc.children))
            continue
        if not line.strip(" \t"):
            finish_paragraph()
            i += 1
            continue
        marker = _list_marker(line)
        if marker:
            indent, marker_type, ordered, start, content_column, rest, nonempty = marker
            # Lists may interrupt paragraphs only with a nonempty item; ordered
            # lists that interrupt must begin at one.
            if paragraph and (not nonempty or (ordered and start != 1)):
                paragraph.append(line)
                i += 1
                continue
            finish_paragraph()
            items: list[Block] = []
            list_loose = False
            while i < len(lines):
                current = _list_marker(lines[i])
                if not current or current[1] != marker_type or current[2] != ordered:
                    break
                item_indent, _, _, _, item_column, item_rest, _ = current
                item_lines = [item_rest]
                i += 1
                saw_blank = False
                while i < len(lines):
                    nxt = _list_marker(lines[i])
                    if nxt and nxt[1] == marker_type and nxt[2] == ordered and nxt[0] < item_column:
                        break
                    if not lines[i].strip(" \t"):
                        # A blank line only belongs to the item when the next
                        # block is sufficiently indented or another sibling
                        # item. Otherwise it separates the list from following
                        # document content and must not loosen the list.
                        look = i + 1
                        while look < len(lines) and not lines[look].strip(" \t"):
                            look += 1
                        next_marker = _list_marker(lines[look]) if look < len(lines) else None
                        if not item_rest.strip(" \t"):
                            if next_marker and next_marker[1] == marker_type and next_marker[2] == ordered and next_marker[0] < item_column:
                                list_loose = True
                                saw_blank = True
                                item_lines.append("")
                                i += 1
                                continue
                            break
                        if next_marker and next_marker[1] == marker_type and next_marker[2] == ordered and next_marker[0] < item_column:
                            list_loose = True
                            saw_blank = True
                            item_lines.append("")
                            i += 1
                            continue
                        next_leading = 0
                        if look < len(lines):
                            for char in lines[look]:
                                if char == " ": next_leading += 1
                                elif char == "\t": next_leading += 4 - next_leading % 4
                                else: break
                        if look < len(lines) and next_leading >= item_column:
                            saw_blank = True
                            item_lines.append("")
                            i += 1
                            continue
                        break
                    leading = 0
                    for char in lines[i]:
                        if char == " ":
                            leading += 1
                        elif char == "\t":
                            leading += 4 - leading % 4
                        else:
                            break
                    if leading >= item_column:
                        continuation, _ = _strip_columns(lines[i], item_column)
                        item_lines.append(continuation)
                        i += 1
                        continue
                    if saw_blank:
                        break
                    # Lazy continuation is allowed only for an open paragraph.
                    if not item_lines or not item_lines[-1].strip(" \t"):
                        break
                    if _thematic(lines[i]) or _atx(lines[i]) or _list_marker(lines[i]) or parse_fenced_code(lines[i:]) or parse_html_block(lines[i:]):
                        break
                    item_lines.append(lines[i])
                    i += 1
                item_doc = parse_blocks("\n".join(item_lines).strip("\n"))
                document.references.update(item_doc.references)
                has_nested_list = any(child.kind == "list" for child in item_doc.children)
                paragraph_after_nested = any(
                    child.kind == "paragraph" for child in item_doc.children[
                        next((index + 1 for index, child in enumerate(item_doc.children) if child.kind == "list"), len(item_doc.children)):
                    ]
                )
                # A nested list following an item's opening paragraph keeps
                # that paragraph's block boundary in the rendered list item.
                if saw_blank and (
                    not item_doc.children
                    # A blank line before a nested list belongs to that
                    # nested structure. It does not make this item's opening
                    # paragraph loose; only a blank between sibling blocks
                    # at the item's own level does.
                    or (any(child.kind == "paragraph" for child in item_doc.children) and (not has_nested_list or paragraph_after_nested))
                ):
                    list_loose = True
                items.append(Block(kind="item", children=item_doc.children))
            document.children.append(Block(kind="list", children=items, ordered=ordered, start=start, tight=not list_loose))
            continue
        setext = parse_setext([*paragraph, line]) if paragraph else None

import html
import re

_LABEL = re.compile(r"^ {0,3}\[([^\[\]]+)\]:[ \t]*(.*)$")


def _unescape(value: str) -> str:
    value = html.unescape(value)
    return re.sub(r"\\([!\"#$%&'()*+,\-./:;<=>?@\[\\\]^_`{|}~])", r"\1", value)


def _label(value: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(value.casefold().strip(" \t\r\n").split())


def extract_definitions(text: str, references: dict) -> str:
    lines = text.splitlines(keepends=True)
    offset = 0
    while offset < len(lines):
        current = lines[offset].rstrip("\r\n")
        match = _LABEL.match(current)
        if not match or not match.group(1).strip(" \t"):
            break
        key = _label(match.group(1))
        first_definition = key not in references
        rest = match.group(2).strip(" \t")
        # Destinations and titles may continue on following lines. Keep the
        # original indentation available while applying the CommonMark limits.
        if not rest and offset + 1 < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[offset + 1].strip(" \t\r\n")
            if candidate:
                rest = candidate
                offset += 1
        if rest and rest[0] in "\"'(" and rest[-1] != ({'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[rest[0]]) and offset + 1 < len(lines):
            candidate = lines[offset + 1].strip(" \t\r\n")
            if candidate:
                rest += " " + candidate
                offset += 1
        destination = None
        title = None
        if rest.startswith("<"):
            end = rest.find(">")
            if end > 0 and "\n" not in rest[1:end]:
                destination, tail = rest[1:end], rest[end + 1:].strip(" \t")
                separated = end + 1 == len(rest) or rest[end + 1].isspace()
            else:
                break
        else:
            dest_match = re.match(r"((?:\\.|[^\s])*)", rest)
            destination = dest_match.group(1) if dest_match else ""
            tail = rest[len(destination):].strip(" \t")
            separated = len(destination) == len(rest) or rest[len(destination)].isspace()
            if destination.count("(") - destination.count(")") > 0:
                break
        if not destination and not (rest.startswith("<") and rest.startswith("<>")):
            break
        if tail:
            if not separated or tail[0] not in "\"'(" or tail[-1] != ({'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[tail[0]]):
                break
            title = _unescape(tail[1:-1])
        if first_definition:
            references[key] = (_unescape(destination), title)
        offset += 1
        if offset < len(lines) and lines[offset].lstrip(" \t").startswith(("\"", "'", "(")) and title is None:
            candidate = lines[offset].strip(" \t\r\n")
            if len(candidate) >= 2 and candidate[0] in "\"'(" and candidate[-1] == {'"': '"', "'": "'", "(": ")"}[candidate[0]]:
                if first_definition:
                    references[key] = (_unescape(destination), _unescape(candidate[1:-1]))
                offset += 1
    return "".join(lines[offset:])

from dataclasses import dataclass
import html
import re

from .inlines import Inline, parse_inlines


@dataclass
class LinkNode:
    type: str
    literal: str = ""
    destination: str = ""
    title: str | None = None
    children: list[Inline | "LinkNode"] | None = None


_ESCAPE = re.compile(r"\\([!\"#$%&'()*+,\-./:;<=>?@\[\\\]^_`{|}~])")
_ENTITY = re.compile(r"&(?:#[xX][0-9A-Fa-f]{1,6}|#[0-9]{1,7}|[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]+);")


def _decode(value: str) -> str:
    value = _ESCAPE.sub(r"\1", value)
    return _ENTITY.sub(lambda m: html.unescape(m.group()), value)


def _normalize_label(label: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(label.casefold().split())


def _destination_and_title(source: str, start: int) -> tuple[str, str | None, int] | None:
    """Parse the contents after an opening parenthesis; return end after ')' ."""
    i, n = start, len(source)
    while i < n and source[i] in " \t\n\r":
        i += 1
    destination = ""
    if i < n and source[i] == "<":
        i += 1
        part: list[str] = []
        while i < n:
            if source[i] == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
                part.extend((source[i], source[i + 1])); i += 2; continue
            if source[i] == "<" or source[i] in "\r\n":
                return None
            if source[i] == ">":
                i += 1; destination = _decode("".join(part)); break
            part.append(source[i]); i += 1
        else:
            return None
    else:
        depth, part = 0, []
        while i < n:
            c = source[i]
            if c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
                part.extend((c, source[i + 1])); i += 2; continue
            if c in " \t\n\r":
                break
            if c == "(":
                depth += 1
                if depth > 32: return None
            elif c == ")":
                if depth == 0: break
                depth -= 1
            part.append(c); i += 1
        if depth:
            return None
        destination = _decode("".join(part))
    whitespace = i
    while i < n and source[i] in " \t\n\r":
        i += 1
    separated = i > whitespace
    title = None
    if i < n and source[i] in "\"'(":
        opener = source[i]; closer = ")" if opener == "(" else opener
        i += 1; part = []
        while i < n:
            c = source[i]
            if c == "\\" and i + 1 < n:
                part.extend((c, source[i + 1])); i += 2; continue
            if c == closer:
                title = _decode("".join(part)); i += 1; break
            if c in "\r\n" and opener != "(":
                return None
            part.append(c); i += 1
        else:
            return None
        if not separated:  # title must be separated from destination
            return None
        while i < n and source[i] in " \t\n\r": i += 1
    if i >= n or source[i] != ")":
        return None
    return destination, title, i + 1


def _bracket_end(source: str, opening: int) -> int | None:
    depth, i = 1, opening + 1
    while i < len(source):
        if source[i] == "`":
            run_end = i + 1
            while run_end < len(source) and source[run_end] == "`":
                run_end += 1
            run = source[i:run_end]
            close = source.find(run, run_end)
            if close >= 0:
                i = close + len(run)
                continue
        if source[i] == "\\":
            i += 2; continue
        if source[i] == "[": depth += 1
        elif source[i] == "]":
            depth -= 1
            if depth == 0: return i
        i += 1
    return None


def parse_links(source: str, references: dict) -> list[Inline | LinkNode]:
    """Parse links from inline source using an already collected reference map."""
    result: list[Inline | LinkNode] = []
    text: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if text:
            result.append(Inline("text", "".join(text)))
            text.clear()

    i = 0
    while i < len(source):
        # Code spans have precedence over brackets, so their contents cannot
        # start a link (nor can a bracket inside a link label close a span).
        if source[i] == "`":
            run_end = i + 1
            while run_end < len(source) and source[run_end] == "`":
                run_end += 1
            run = source[i:run_end]
            close = source.find(run, run_end)
            if close >= 0:
                end = close + len(run)
                text.append(source[i:end])
                i = end
                continue
        if source[i] == "\\" and i + 1 < len(source):
            text.extend(source[i:i + 2]); i += 2; continue
        if source[i] != "[" or (i and source[i - 1] == "!"):
            text.append(source[i]); i += 1; continue
        close = _bracket_end(source, i)
        if close is None:
            text.append(source[i]); i += 1; continue
        label_source = source[i + 1:close]
        parsed: tuple[str, str | None, int] | None = None
        after = close + 1
        if after < len(source) and source[after] == "(":
            parsed = _destination_and_title(source, after + 1)
        if parsed is not None:
            dest, title, end = parsed
        else:
            reference_label = label_source
            end = after
            if after < len(source) and source[after] == "[":
                ref_close = _bracket_end(source, after)
                if ref_close is not None:
                    reference_label = source[after + 1:ref_close] or label_source
                    end = ref_close + 1
            entry = references.get(_normalize_label(_decode(reference_label)))
            if entry is None:
                text.append(source[i]); i += 1; continue
            if isinstance(entry, dict):
                dest, title = entry.get("destination", ""), entry.get("title")
            else:
                dest, title = entry[0], entry[1] if len(entry) > 1 else None
        flush()
        result.append(LinkNode("link", destination=dest, title=title,
                               children=parse_inlines(label_source, {})))
        i = end
    flush()
    return result

    """Render inline constructs, keeping code and raw HTML opaque."""
    pieces: list[str] = []
    for token in parse_inline_html_breaks(source):

            pieces.append("<br />\n")
            continue
        if token.type == "html":
            pieces.append(token.literal)
            continue

        links = parse_links(token.literal, references)

            if item.type == "link":
                label = "".join(_render_inline_node(n, references) for n in (item.children or []))

                destination = quote(item.destination, safe="/:?#@!$&'()*+,;=%-._~")
                pieces.append(f'<a href="{escape(destination, quote=True)}"{title}>{label}</a>')

                pieces.extend(_render_text_with_images(item.literal, references))

            if close is not None:

                after = close + 1

                    title_attr = f' title="{escape(title, quote=True)}"' if title is not None else ""
                    dest = quote(dest, safe="/:?#@!$&'()*+,;=%-._~")
                    out.append(f'<img src="{escape(dest, quote=True)}" alt="{escape(_plain_alt(alt, references), quote=True)}"{title_attr} />')
                    i = end; continue
                ref = alt
                end = after
                if after < len(source) and source[after] == "[":
                    rc = _bracket_end(source, after)
                    if rc is not None:
                        ref = source[after + 1:rc] or alt; end = rc + 1
                entry = references.get(_normalize_label(_decode(ref)))
                if entry is not None:
                    dest, title = (entry.get("destination", ""), entry.get("title")) if isinstance(entry, dict) else (entry[0], entry[1] if len(entry) > 1 else None)

                    dest = quote(dest, safe="/:?#@!$&'()*+,;=%-._~")

def _render_plain(source: str, references: dict) -> str:
    # Recognize autolinks before escape processing. An escaped punctuation mark
    # inside a URI is part of the URI source and must not split its token.
    result: list[str] = []
    for auto in parse_autolinks(source):
        if auto.type == "link":
            destination = quote(auto.destination, safe=":/?#@!$&'()*+,;=%-._~")
            result.append(f'<a href="{escape(destination, quote=True)}">{escape(auto.label, quote=True)}</a>')
        else:
            result.append("".join(_render_inline_node(node, references) for node in parse_inlines(auto.literal, references)))

def _render_inline_node(node, references: dict) -> str:
    if node.type == "text": return escape(node.literal, quote=True)
    if node.type == "escaped": return escape(node.literal, quote=True)
    if node.type == "entity": return escape(node.literal, quote=True)
    if node.type == "code": return f"<code>{escape(node.literal, quote=True)}</code>"
    if node.type == "softbreak": return "\n"
    if node.type == "em": return "<em>" + "".join(_render_inline_node(n, references) for n in node.children or []) + "</em>"
    if node.type == "strong": return "<strong>" + "".join(_render_inline_node(n, references) for n in node.children or []) + "</strong>"
    return escape(getattr(node, "literal", ""), quote=False)


def _render_block(block, references: dict, tight: bool) -> str:
    if block.kind == "paragraph":
        body = _render_inlines(block.literal, references)
        return body + "\n" if tight else f"<p>{body}</p>\n"
    if block.kind == "heading":
        return f"<h{block.level}>{_render_inlines(block.literal, references)}</h{block.level}>\n"
    if block.kind == "thematic_break": return "<hr />\n"
    if block.kind == "fenced_code":
        info = block.info.split(None, 1)[0] if block.info else ""
        info = unescape(re.sub(r"\\([!\"#$%&'()*+,\-./:;<=>?@\[\\\]^_`{|}~])", r"\1", info))

    if block.kind == "indented_code": return f"<pre><code>{escape(block.literal, quote=True)}</code></pre>\n"
    if block.kind == "html_block": return block.literal
    if block.kind == "block_quote":

        # children; paragraphs inside a nested quote retain their tags.
        inner = "".join(_render_block(child, references, False) for child in block.children)
        return "<blockquote>\n" + inner + "</blockquote>\n"
    if block.kind == "list":
        tag = "ol" if block.ordered else "ul"
        attr = f' start="{block.start}"' if block.ordered and block.start != 1 else ""
        def render_item(item):
            parts = []
            for child in item.children:

                else:
                    parts.append(_render_block(child, references, False))
            return "<li>" + "".join(parts) + "</li>\n"
        body = "".join(render_item(item) for item in block.children)
        return f"<{tag}{attr}>\n{body}</{tag}>\n"
    return ""
